en: You're sure?
Mhm. I wasn't lying when I said I hate street racers. You show those Devil Killers who's boss, okay?
Heheh. Strange though, how so many talented drivers end up being drawn to our company. I guess that's all the chief's doing.
What? Didn't you know? He used to be a street racer himself.
...You're not serious, are you?
Well, all I've heard are rumors. This must've been over two decades ago, and I don't know the details.
(I find that hard to believe, but...)
But despite my loathing for reckless, street-racing jerks, I have nothing but respect for our boss. He's one of the few who made it out of the game to start an honest living.
Anyway, I know I went off without saying anything, so I think it's best we head back. Don't want to keep the chief waiting any longer than I already have!
Good. Let's get a move on.
Guess what, Suzuki-san. I just got a call from Muramatsu-kun. It sounds like he picked up that regular client of his on time!
Did he now?
Yup. Says he was takin' a break in his cab, and dozed off.
We've been busy lately, so I ain't surprised. Now if ya must doze off, Suzuki-san, make sure it ain't when you're behind the wheel⑬not that I expect ya would.
I'll be sure not to.
Good. Wouldn't want any accidents now, that's for sure.
...Hey, Chief?
...Actually, never mind.
Huh. Alrighty then.
How you holdin' up, Hirakawa-san?
I'd be better if my shoulders weren't so stiff...
Yeah? Me too! Shoulders, neck, back, you name it! That's what happens when ya get old.
(This guy used to be a street racer...?)
<Color:22>Nagasugawa Street<Color:Default>, if you would.
(I've seen this guy on TV⑬he's a member of the Diet. They think he could be the next prime minister.)
Phew. Going out to meet supporters sure is tiring.
That does sound tough.
Yes, but it's my electorate, so what can you do? Who did you vote for in the last election?
You, of course.
Oh yeah? Good to hear it. Which of my policies do you support?
You didn't really vote for me, did you?
No. I'm afraid I only moved here six months ago.
Hmph. You've got some cheek, lying to my face like that!
(Looks like I made him angry.)
I'm afraid I only moved here six months ago.
Oh yeah? With so many people leaving these days, it's always good to see new blood moving in.
I hope you pump some new life into Fukuoka!
(He looks pleased.)
I'm not all that interested in politics.
Well, at least you're honest. That said...
You really should read up a little more. You need to be able to discuss all kinds of things in your job.
You're right. I'll brush up.
I'm thinking about incorporating ideas from the public in my campaign.
What do you think the biggest problem is today?
Hmm. I do think it's harder for young people to hold onto their hopes and dreams these days.
Right. That worries me, as well. There's too many kids out fooling around instead of working.
But I don't know what they're thinking, and they don't seem to want to listen to adults like me.
What do you do when young people aren't even willing to hear you out?
If they won't listen to you, why not beat some sense into them?
That'll only make things worse. They'll turn their backs on us completely.
These days most kids have never even had a spanking from their parents.
It doesn't seem like your idea is very realistic.
Maybe you could present yourself in a way that caters to their tastes?
Hmm. That's a point, but I don't know...
Politics should be genuine, not just a performance. Putting on an act solves nothing.
I see. It is tricky.
How about listening to them first?
Huh? You think I should listen to young people?
You complain that they don't hear you out, but have you been giving them a voice to speak with?
Now that you mention it, I don't remember talking to many young people in the past.
But we're just not on the same wavelength. It's like they're a whole different species.
When you were young, didn't you get sick of being ignored by those who were older than you?
Well, I did do my fair share of partying. That never went down well with my parents.
When I think about it, maybe the youth of today aren't so different from me.
All right! I'll try giving them a chance to share their opinions and hear them out.
Then maybe they'll be more willing to listen to me as well!
I like the way you think, driver! Thanks for the tip!
Happy to be of service.
Thank you for the ride. I'll give you a big tip if you promise to back me in the election.
I don't take tips like that.
Tips are supposed to be a gesture of appreciation.
Ha. You're straight as an arrow, aren't you?
If there were more people like you around here, there might actually be some hope for this country.
That depends on how big the tip is.
Hmm. How much are we talking?
For my vote? 10,000 yen.
Ha! Don't make me laugh.
I'm always curious to see whether guys like you would take a bribe or turn it down. That's the only reason I said that.
I picked you as someone who couldn't be bought. I guess I was wrong, though.
I'll take the tip, but my vote can't be bought.
If I voted for you, it could be seen as bribery.
Well, if you feel that way, you should just turn down the tip altogether.
I picked you as someone who would turn me down flat. I guess I was wrong, though.
Much appreciated! Here's the fare, and a little extra as a tip!
Hahaha. Go on, take it. You've really brightened up my day!
This is just a token of my gratitude.
See you next time!
Much appreciated! That was a fun ride. Here's the fare!
You know, after talking to you, I'm a little worried about the future of this country.
Oh. I'm sorry to hear that.
Ah, well. I guess it's my job to solve those problems. Keep your nose to the grindstone.
Can you take me to my office on <Color:22>Meisei Street<Color:Default> ASAP!? If I'm late today they'll fire me!
Okay. But you look pale. Is everything all right?
Well, I really need to use the restroom... But first I have to punch in at work!
Oh, then let's go.
Hurry, please!
Yay! I made it to work on time! And it's all thanks to you.
Happy to help. Didn't you need to be somewhere...?
Oh yeah! I'd better head off now. Thanks!
Well, looks like we made it! I'd better dash to the restroom!
Thank you for choosing Nagasu Taxi.
No, thank you! Bye!
This is the worst day of my life. I've never been so humiliated.
Now I have no job, and... Oh, never mind. I don't want to talk about it. Bye.
Hey, mom. Why's the sea blue?
I'm afraid I don't know, sweetie.
Come on, let's get in the taxi. Could you take us to <Color:22>Meisei Street<Color:Default> please?
What a nice man!
We felt safe with you behind the wheel.
(It seems they enjoyed the ride.)
Thank you. Sorry about this little blabbermouth.
Not at all. Hope to see you again.
Can't you see I'm with a child here!? You need to be more considerate!
(They don't exactly seem thrilled with their service. I'll have to be more careful.)
You sure took your time! Ooh well, well! Aren't you a handsome one?
(This guy has a pretty feminine way of speaking.)
Aww gee, mister. I get carsick when I sit in the back. Could I possibly sit in the front with you?
I don't think that's really the case. But you're welcome to take the back seat.
Uh?
Don't gimme that crap!
(Whoa. His voice is a lot deeper all of a sudden.)
I'm a payin' customer here! Where do ya get off callin' me a liar!?
I swear, I hear any more of that outta you, and I'm gonna put in a complaint with the taxi bureau! Ya got it, pal!?
(It's like Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. I better watch what I say.)
I'm very sorry.
When we carry a single passenger, the rules state that we have to ask them to sit in the back. Would you mind?
Hmph. I guess I'll have to now, won't I?
(Seems I managed to calm him back down.)
Ugh, you're such a fine looking man, I find it hard to resist your commands!
Hehe! Oh, I just love that serious look on your face!
I'm sorry, but there are rules. I'm afraid that when we carry a single passenger, we have to ask that they sit in the back.
I hope that's all right with you.
Oh, you're such a party pooper.
But I do find it hard to resist the commands of such a fine-looking man!
I'm afraid you'll have to call another taxi.
What!? No way! Are you refusing to give me a ride?
Unfortunately. I apologize.
I'm a payin' customer! You refuse me a ride, I'll report ya to the taxi bureau!
(It's like Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. I guess I'll take him, but rules are he sits in the back.)
But for safety reasons, I'll have to ask you to sit in the back. Would you mind?
Ugh, you're such a fine looking man, I find it hard to resist your commands! In the back I go.
Can I ask your name, driver?
It's Taichi Suzuki.
Then I'll call you Ta-kun! What's your blood type, Ta-kun?
It's type O.
No way! I'm type B! Did you know that type O and type B people are really compatible?
I didn't.
Perhaps fate has brought us together! What do you think?
I'll have to disagree.
You're a taxi driver, ain't ya? You're supposed to make small talk, ya idiot!
You'll have to forgive me. I'm still pretty new at this. I'll be more careful.
Oh, that's all right, Ta-kun.
You're such a cutie pie, I'll give you a pass!
There are plenty of people with type O blood out there. After type A, it's the most common in Japan.
Aww, now you've gone and spoiled the mood, Ta-kun. Couldn't you have at least played along a bit?
Oh, well. You're such a cutie pie, I'll give you a pass!
I think fate plays a part in all encounters. Blood type doesn't really come into it.
That sounds so pretentious, Ta-kun! But I like it! You're really getting me steamed up.
We'll be there soon.
Oh, that's a shame! I wanted to spend more time talking to you, Ta-kun.
How about we go out for tea or something?
Call me for a long distance drive next time. Then we can talk plenty.
Really!? Maybe I will, hehe!
Yeah right, like hell I will!
You moneygrubbin' prick! I'm not amused! You're no escort, ya know!? It's only tea!
Right, but⑬
I've just about had it with you! Ya think you're hot stuff, just 'cause your looks are above average!
(I seem to have made him angry. He's like a different person when he gets worked up.)
Drivers aren't here to talk with clients.
I see. I suppose you're right. Your job is to drive, isn't it?
I bet if I was a pretty girl, you'd be happy to chat with me all day long, asshole!
Small talk is part of the job, too, ya know!? Ya gotta be able to make conversation with any client!
I have more work to do. Maybe some other time.
Aww. You're such a hard worker, Ta-kun.
Well, I like this job.
(Uh-oh. Did I make him mad?)
I just got shot with Cupid's arrow! You say the most beautiful things, Ta-kun. I'm in love!
Well, I wouldn't want to get in the way of your work, Ta-kun.
It really is a shame, but it looks like this is goodbye for now. Mind if I ask for you again?
Of course not.
I haven't met a man of your caliber for a while. My little heart is pounding away!
Mmm, I hope you'll let me sit up front next time!
Uh, I'm afraid that⑬
I'm only joking! But I will ask for you again! I had a great ride, so you deserve a tip!
Until next time, Ta-kun! Mwah!
I'm just kidding! Here's the fare!
Until next time, Ta-kun!
You know, at first I thought you were my type, but you're really not all that. You need to work on your manners.
Well, bye-bye.
(That was one tough customer...)
(Wow. They sure are well coordinated.)
To <Color:22>Ose Bridge Street<Color:Default>, please!
Hey, it's our three month anniversary!
We're going to be together forever, Ken-kun!
I feel like we were made for each other, Mi-tan.
I was just thinking the same thing!
(A couple of love birds.)
Hmm? Why are you peeking at us in the mirror?
I was just thinking how lucky you both are.
Hahaha. People stare at us on the street a lot, too.
They're just jealous of how in love we are.
Don't worry, driver. You'll find your soul mate soon enough. Just like me and Mi-tan!
(They're in a good mood.)
I was just thinking how annoying you both are.
I bet you're single, right? You must be jealous that we have it so good.
You really ought to grow up, mister.
I agree!
(That didn't make them too happy.)
No, I was just checking the cars behind us.
Oh, I see. Sorry.
I just thought you might have your eye on my gorgeous girl here.
Aww, you're embarrassing me, Ken-kun!
It's true! I could stare at your beautiful face all day, Mi-tan!
